chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a young boy who had not yet reached ten years of age, who committed zina with a woman, he عليه السلام said: “The boy is lashed short of the hadd, and the woman is given the hadd in full.”
I said: “What if she was muḥṣanah?” He عليه السلام said: “She is not stoned, because the one who had intercourse with her is not mature. But if he had been mature, she would have been stoned.”

key_terms.دُونَ الْحَدِّ: less than the full prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.غُلَامٍ صَغِيرٍ: a young boy who has not reached maturity
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِمُدْرِكٍ: not legally mature / not having reached discernment
key_terms.مُحْصَنَةً: a married or otherwise legally fortified woman in the context of zina law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a prepubescent boy commits zina with a woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning zina involving a boy who has not yet reached the age of legal maturity. It distinguishes between the lesser disciplinary punishment of the boy and the full hadd for the woman, while clarifying that rajm does not apply to a muḥṣanah in this case because the boy is not yet mudrik.
